name: Neo-Zionism
summary: Neo-Zionism, a term popularised by sociologist Uri Ram, names the right-wing, religious-nationalist current that grew in Israel after the 1967 war. It treats the whole biblical Land of Israel, including the West Bank and Gaza, as Jewish land to be settled and kept, makes Judaism central to the state, and is hostile to territorial compromise. Critics describe it as exclusionary and antidemocratic, while some adherents embrace the label.
scope: The post-1967 religious-nationalist settler current as described by Ram and the Wikipedia article, centred on Gush Emunim and the teachings of Tzvi Yehuda Kook (and Abraham Isaac Kook) and extending to parties such as Moledet and Tehiya and groups such as Kumah and Im Tirtzu. Excludes classical Labour or liberal Zionism and the Kahanist transfer programme as a whole; Kahanism is treated as a neighbouring strand. No single canonical program exists, so many answers on economics and social issues are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Zvi Yehuda Kook
keyFigures.role: Rabbi whose teachings inspired Gush Emunim and led it from 1974

keyFigures.name: Uri Ram
keyFigures.role: Sociologist who popularised the term Neo-Zionism in a 1996 essay

keyFigures.name: Yishai Fleisher
keyFigures.role: Arutz Sheva broadcaster who founded the Kumah neo-Zionist lobby and defends the label

sources.usedFor: Settlement aims in the West Bank, Gaza and Golan; messianic and halachic-state ideas; rejection of Kahane's transfer proposals

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The ideology is defined by land and identity, not economics; Likud-aligned and settler-sector adherents are split between market and state-backed settlement funding.

public-ownership.rationale: Nothing in the sources endorses nationalisation; adherents aligned with Likud and the national-religious camp have generally accepted privatisation, an inference only.

unions-good.rationale: The ideology has no recorded stance on organised labour; adherents' economic views vary.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Economic regulation is outside the ideology's concerns as documented; adherents are split.

cut-welfare.rationale: No documented position; the national-religious camp has mixed views and relies on state support for settlements and yeshivot.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement is strongly statist about the Jewish state, which Kook held was a step in redemption, so it rejects abolishing the state.

empower-police-military.rationale: The ideology treats the Arab-Israeli conflict as existential and backs settlement under military protection, so adherents favour a stronger security apparatus.

traditional-family.rationale: The movement's religious core is Orthodox and ties national redemption to Torah observance; traditional family values follow from this.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Adherents are drawn from Orthodox and national-religious circles that treat Torah law as binding, which excludes same-sex marriage.

more-religion-public.rationale: Ram describes the trend as treating Judaism as central rather than peripheral, and Gush Emunim's slogan sets the Land of Israel for the people of Israel according to the Torah of Israel.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Ram frames the trend around Jewish national-historic destiny and Judaism's central role, and the Gush Emunim slogan puts Torah at the centre of national life.

gradual-change.rationale: Kook and Gush Emunim pushed rapid settlement facts and treated redemption as an active process; this cuts against deference to established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Ram notes support for barring non-Jewish immigration, but the ideology also champions Jewish aliyah, so a literal answer is split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Gush Emunim held that no government foreign or Israeli may block settlement, and Kook counted seeking gentile approval as an offence to God.

nation-first.rationale: Ram describes a nationalist, exclusionary trend, and Kook held that God's desire for the Land overrides any outside negotiation.

open-borders.rationale: Ram describes support for a Jewish-majority ethnic-religious state and for barring non-Jewish immigration, which excludes eventually open borders.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: None of the sources links technology to the ideology's goals, so adherents have no distinctive view on technological optimism.

revolution-justified.rationale: Gush Emunim members defied government policy and the 1984 underground used violence, but Kook also disapproved of coercion, so adherents are split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolition of money and wage labour is a Marxist-communist aim with no place in a religious-nationalist right-wing ideology.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The movement's messianic rhetoric invokes a restored biblical kingdom among militants, but mainstream adherents work within a republic; mild inference.

democracy-best.rationale: Ram calls the trend antidemocratic, and Kook held Torah prescriptions cannot be overturned by referendum, so democracy is not treated as supreme.

direct-votes.rationale: Kook considered referendums illegitimate where they could override Torah, a direct source for scepticism of plebiscites on major questions.

workers-councils.rationale: Council communism has no connection to a religious-nationalist right-wing ideology.

right-to-secede.rationale: The trend insists the whole Land stays under Israeli sovereignty and rejects dividing it, so regional secession is rejected.

political-violence-never.rationale: Gush Emunim's mainstream rejected violence in principle, but the militant wing and the 1984 underground did not, and Kook endorsed force against Arab war; so absolutism is rejected.

separate-church-state.rationale: Gush Emunim's ideas are described as halachic-state oriented, and Kook held Torah law takes precedence over secular law.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Kook ranked Torah above secular law and Gush Emunim is associated with the idea of a halachic state, though not every adherent demands full halakhic legislation.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Defence is a core state-security task for a movement that sees the conflict as existential.

military-superiority.rationale: Ram describes a security-centred reading of Arab hostility, and settlement was justified partly because pre-1967 borders were indefensible.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Ram describes exclusionary Jewish nationalism seeking a state of Jews, though the framing is religious-national rather than purely ethnic.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class conflict as history's engine is Marxist and opposed to the national-religious view that history is a redemptive process.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Adherents claim indigenous status for Jews and deny Arab national rights to the land, per Kook, so the principle as usually meant is not endorsed.

restore-past-order.rationale: Gush Emunim aimed to return Jews to the biblical homeland and biblical-style order, but it also embraced modern statehood; so only a weak lean.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The movement treated settlement as a religious duty regardless of cost, which cuts against judging policy only by results.

direct-action.rationale: Settlement outposts and defying government limits were Gush Emunim's central tactic, though it also entered electoral politics.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A Marxist-utopian aim outside the ideology.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Marxist exploitation theory has no place in the ideology.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist theory with no support in the sources.

harm-principle.rationale: Kook placed Torah above secular law, so liberal limits on state restriction are not the adherent standard.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Ram describes the trend as treating the Jewish people as a collective with national-historic destiny; rights are not individual only.

state-as-business.rationale: Kook treated the state as a vehicle of redemption, not a business serving customers.

total-state.rationale: The ideology is nationalist and statist about the Land, but sources do not describe a total state; religious autonomy stays important.

national-rebirth.rationale: Gush Emunim and Kook saw return to the Land and Torah as redemptive renewal, countering secular decadence, though the sources do not use "decadence" language.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Ram says the trend advocates unlimited Jewish settlement of the West Bank and Gaza and treats all territory under Israeli control as part of the Land; Gush Emunim sought settlement in the West Bank, Gaza and Golan.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal oaths are unrelated to the ideology.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The Gush Emunim slogan sets the Land of Israel for the people of Israel, and Ram describes the trend as seeing the Jewish state as a national-historic destiny in the Land.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Fleisher says the Jewish people are not yet back home, and Gush Emunim's redemptive vision requires ingathering of Jews to the Land.

economic-freedom.rationale: The sources do not tie political freedom to economic freedom, and the ideology is not defined by economic liberalism.

national-self-determination.rationale: Adherents claim the right for the Jewish nation but, per Kook, deny Arab national rights to the Land, so the universal principle is applied selectively.

force-without-un.rationale: Gush Emunim held no foreign government may block settlement and Ram's account stresses unilateral security; adherents back force without UN approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Kook and Gush Emunim ground policy in Torah and divine redemption, not in reason alone.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: An accelerationist cultural statement with no basis in the ideology.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Ram describes exclusionary politics toward Arabs, but not a racial caste law; sources do not support racial segregation by law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist theory of the state has no place in the ideology.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production policy is outside what the sources say about the ideology.

elite-replacement.rationale: Ram records the demographic-threat framing about Arabs, but not a deliberate elite replacement plot.

national-mission.rationale: Fisch's claim that Jews have a unique mission and should not behave like an ordinary nation is documented in the movement, though the statement's spread of government form is not.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Orthodox-aligned adherents reject the feminist structural claim.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The movement depends on a state that funds and defends settlement, so a minimal state is not its aim.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Kook allowed Arabs who accept Jewish sovereignty to remain as a minority, but Ram describes exclusionary and racist tendencies; adherents split on equal rights.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Marxist-Leninist debate with no connection to the ideology.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Neo-Zionist adherents reject the colonial label; Kook denied that Arabs had a national right to the land and held Jews were returning to their own homeland.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not an issue for the ideology.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The movement spread through religious schools and state-religious education and wants Torah in schooling.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is a Soviet-era doctrine about a socialist state, which the sources never connect to Neo-Zionism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Kook held authority rests on Torah, not consent, and rejected referendums where Torah forbids.

population-transfer.rationale: Ram records that some in the trend advocate transfer by agreement, while Gush Emunim's mainstream rejected the transfer proposals of Meir Kahane; adherents are split.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Kook held force justified against Arab war and the movement seized land; the principle is rejected.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Adherents oppose bans on Kahane-style parties yet also back bans on anti-Zionist ones; Kook defended Kahane's right to a voice in the Knesset.

separated-powers.rationale: Ram describes hostility to the courts as limits on the nation's Jewish character; Kook put Torah above institutions.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing sales are a UK policy issue that the sources never connect to the ideology.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Ram describes the trend's view that coexistence with Arabs is an illusion and its focus on a Jewish national-religious coalition.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Gush Emunim held no foreign government may block settlement, and Kook said seeking gentile approval offends God; pooling sovereignty is rejected.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist slogan opposed to a nationalist ideology.

people-in-arms.rationale: Settlers' armed self-defence is documented, but replacing the army is not.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Fisch argued Jews have a unique mission and should not behave like an ordinary nation, which rejects strict cultural equality.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Kook said surrendering territory was as forbidden as eating pork and opposed Begin's Egypt talks as treason, and his 1967 speech asked whether any part of the Land could be given up; Gush Emunim aimed to make a land-for-peace deal unworkable.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The nature of the Soviet economy is an issue the sources do not link to this ideology.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Ram describes the trend as treating the territories as part of Israel and the Land, so annexed land with a hostile population is not regarded as unlawfully occupied.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Kook held Torah and its authorities outrank the state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Kook treated the state as holy but denied divinity of rulers; Jewish theology rejects divine rulers.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Kook held Torah law binds the state and rulers.

refugee-return.rationale: Ram describes the trend's rejection of Arab claims and Kook's denial that Palestinians were expelled in 1948 and that Arabs have a national right to the land; return of refugees is rejected.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The trend's claim to the biblical Land rests on Jewish ancestry and Torah, covering territory where Jews have a historical tie.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The movement's premise is that Jews must be ingathered to the Land of Israel, not struggle for equal rights in the diaspora; Fleisher says the Jewish people are not yet back home.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Kook read history as a divine redemptive process, not economic determination.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Ram's trend is hostile to liberal-democratic limits, and Kook said Torah law, not courts, bounds authority; yet adherents often resist the Israeli Supreme Court, which supports this answer.

moral-incentives.rationale: A Maoist-communist idea unrelated to the sources.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Settler action against government policy was documented, but the foco theory of revolution is not part of the doctrine.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Ram's account centres Jewish national-historic destiny and yeshiva networks transmit religious-national history, so adherents want nation-centred teaching.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Kook denied Arabs a national right to the land, but the sources do not describe a civilising-mission doctrine.

patriotic-education.rationale: Gush Emunim spread its influence through religious schools and yeshivot, and its nationalist ethos favours instilling loyalty to the Jewish state.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Marxist-Leninist thesis with no link to the ideology.

elective-rulers.rationale: No documented position; the movement participates in elections but also asserts Torah authority.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Kook later called the government illegitimate and a tyrannical dictatorship and treated territorial surrender as treason; this supports a right of resistance to rulers who breach Torah.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Kook accepted the Knesset as a venue but said Torah outranks it; no clean position.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Gush Emunim made political activism, settlement and pressure on government its central purpose, and Kook urged students to settle, which rejects withdrawal.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian analysis has no role in the ideology.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is not part of the doctrine.

party-own-road.rationale: This communist-movement question does not apply to the ideology.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Kook's 1967 speech mourned the division of the Land and Hebron, Shechem and Jericho, and he later opposed yielding any territory.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The trend claims Jews as the Land's indigenous people and denies Arab national rights, so it does not endorse the usual form of this principle.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Im Tirtzu, which Ram links to the trend's wider milieu, campaigned against foreign funding of left-wing NGOs; this is an inference from the milieu, not a stated program.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Kook said Torah law outranks state law, but he told followers to obey a court ruling on Arab-owned land; split.

non-intervention.rationale: The sources do not give a general doctrine on non-interference, and adherents reject outside pressure on Israel while favouring hard security action.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Ram says the trend treats Arab opposition as rooted in antisemitism and Arab citizens as a fifth column, but this describes a hostile minority, not a secret conspiracy, so adherents are not clearly agreeing.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Jewish marriage law is central to religious Zionism; abolition would be rejected.

informal-organisation.rationale: Gush Emunim was a loose movement and settlers acted through small groups, but it had formal bodies (Amana, Yesha Council).

national-law-over-international.rationale: Gush Emunim held that no foreign government has the right to block settlement, and Kook rejected foreign approval of Israel's rights over the Land.

religious-nation.rationale: Ram says the trend treats Judaism as central and its claim rests on the Torah; the national community is Jewish by religion and descent.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Kook held that seeking gentile support offends God; submission to another power is rejected.

religion-illusion.rationale: Gush Emunim fused Zionism with messianic Judaism and Kook saw the state as a stage of divine redemption, which is incompatible with calling religion an illusion.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Settlement communities were a Gush Emunim feature but the statement describes a wider reorganisation of society.

majority-settlement.rationale: The trend promotes Jewish settlement of Judea, Samaria and Gaza, regions with a large Arab population; that is majority-group settlement in minority regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The sources do not frame the ideology as a third economic way.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Ram describes land claims resting on the Torah and biblical Land of Israel, and Kook held God's will for the Land's integrity overrides any human negotiation.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The movement is built on Jewish national survival; Ram's account contains no denial and treats Arab hostility as rooted in antisemitism.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Ram calls the trend antidemocratic, but the sources do not describe suppressing opposition as a program.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic doctrine, rejected by a movement that treats Arab opposition as hostile.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: An intersectional framework has no place in the ideology.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Ram places the trend clearly on the right, opposed to Labour Zionism.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Ram describes the trend's view that Arab opposition is rooted in antisemitism and that coexistence is an illusion, which supports a hostile view of Islamic politics though the specific statement is about Western countries.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Kook placed Torah above secular law and Gush Emunim's slogan ends with the Torah of Israel; authority ultimately comes from God.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The ideology holds that Arab opposition is rooted in antisemitism and that settlement must be defended, so abolishing the army is entirely rejected.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Eco-feminist theory is outside the ideology.

racial-franchise.rationale: Ram's trend is exclusionary toward Arabs but defines the nation by Jewishness, and the sources do not show a racial franchise.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Kook treated Torah law as taking precedence and as binding, opposing liberal reinterpretation.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Kook held the Torah supreme and Gush Emunim sought a Jewish religious renewal of the state, which is incompatible with state promotion of atheism.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Ram describes the trend's rejection of coexistence and of coalition with Arab parties; power-sharing with Arabs is refused.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The current focuses on national and religious survival rather than global extinction risk; adherents would be indifferent or split, so this is a neutral inference.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The current is rooted in Orthodox religious Zionism of the Kook school, which reserves rabbinic and communal leadership offices for men.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Kook's teaching and Gush Emunim see an unbroken Jewish bond with the biblical Land of Israel from antiquity to the present.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The current holds that the state exists to gather the Jewish people into the Land, so a diaspora centre alone is not enough.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Gush Emunim saw settlement as religious redemption and the state as a messianic step, so spiritual purpose is central.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The current organises as a religious-national group, not a racial one; the question does not fit it clearly.

collective-bargaining.rationale: No program on labour relations; religious-nationalist supporters are split on unions and markets.

sacred-nation.rationale: Kook's teaching treats the state of Israel as holy and the nation as part of divine redemption.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The sources focus on land and religion, not labor law; adherents are split between religious-nationalist and market-leaning positions.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Adherents prize elections but critics call the current antidemocratic in its rejection of territorial compromise by vote; no clear stated view.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Gush Emunim and Kook treat the whole Land of Israel as holy and settlement as a religious step toward redemption.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Neo-Zionism makes Judaism central to the state and its parties and rabbinic authority religious in form.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Kook held that Torah takes precedence over secular law, and halakha requires the husband's consent to a get.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Kook placed Torah above secular law and Gush Emunim held that no government may bar settlement of the Land, reflecting a higher-law view of authority.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The current is a right-wing religious-nationalist force that rejects communism and one-party socialism; this follows from its definition in the sources.

missingStatements.text: Religious communities should be allowed to settle and build in territory their faith regards as sacred, even where the government restricts it.
missingStatements.rationale: Gush Emunim held that no government has the right to block settlement of the Land and treated settlement as a religious step toward redemption.

missingStatements.text: Arab citizens of a state defined as the homeland of another nation pose a threat to its security and demographic character.
missingStatements.rationale: Ram's account says the trend views Arab citizens as a fifth column and a demographic threat, though this is the trend's most contested element.
missingStatements.declined: Contested and specific to this trend; close to minority-conspiracy and diversity-weakens-cohesion, which already capture the underlying stance.

notes: The label is used both critically (Ram: exclusionary and antidemocratic) and by some self-described proponents. Gush Emunim's mainstream disavowed Kahane-style transfer, while Moledet-type strands endorse transfer by agreement. Hardal and messianic strands would answer religion-and-state items more strongly. Several economic answers are placeholders by inference.
